newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sentences five Moslem militants to death.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sentences five Moslem militants to death.

text.p: Egypt's Supreme State Security Court sentenced five Moslem militants to death on Monday for killing civilians and policemen in the southern Assiut province in 1993.

Two of the militants sentenced by Judge Salah Budour are on the run. They are among a group of 32 people charged with killing 10 policemen, including high-ranking officers, and 10 civilians near Abu Tig town, 345 km (215 miles) south of Cairo.

Security sources said the men went on trial in March also for belonging to the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) and for blasting buildings and shooting at trains in southern Egypt between 1993 to 1994.
They were also charged with illegally possessing weapons.
"The Islamic revival is encroaching... Allah (God) make a staircase of our skulls to your glory," the convicts chanted while waving Korans (Moslem Holy book) in the prosecution cage.
"We are martyrs for Islam," they shouted.
The Gama'a is the largest Moslem militant group fighting to transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state. It targets policemen, Christians, tourists and government officials in its armed campaign.
"I've been expecting this," said Adel Abdel Rahman, a 22-year old farmer who was sentenced to death.
He crumbled to the ground in the prosecution cage after the judge read out the verdict.
"I'm a martyr, I'm a martyr," he shouted gleefully while flinging chocolates and sweets to policemen and reporters. "Please take these sweets to celebrate."
Prosecutors said Abdel Rahman had killed a policeman and a Christian village mayor the Gama'a said had committed adultery.
The others sentenced to death were also convicted of killing, among several others, police Major-General Mohammed el-Shimy and his two assistants, a police major and a lieutenant-colonel.
Wailing relatives screamed words of encouragement at the defendants as police herded them into trucks. As they drove, defendants threw more candy at their sobbing wives and children.
The judge will sentence the remaining 27 defendants on January 6.
Since 1992, about 1,000 people have been killed in political violence. Egypt has also executed at least 53 of the 76 people it has sentenced to death.
